content.title: What Is the Difference Between a Criminal Justice Attorney and a Criminal Defense Attorney?
content.text: Blair Defense Criminal Lawyers | June 10, 2025 | Criminal Defense If you’re involved in a criminal matter, you might be confused about the terms “criminal justice attorney” and “criminal defense attorney.” They sound similar but can mean different things in some contexts. Learning about the differences between the two can help you choose the right type of lawyer for your needs. In this blog post, we’ll explain clearly what each type of attorney does and how they differ. A criminal justice attorney is a lawyer who works in the criminal justice system in a general way. They can serve in many different roles. Some work as prosecutors, who bring criminal charges against people accused of crimes. Others work as judges, making decisions in criminal trials. Criminal justice attorneys can also represent crime victims. They help victims navigate the legal process, understand their rights, and seek fair treatment from the court system. This type of attorney doesn’t always represent the same side. What Does a Criminal Defense Attorney Do? A criminal defense attorney specifically helps people accused of crimes. Their main job is to protect the rights of defendants throughout the entire criminal process. They represent people during investigations, plea deal negotiations, trials, and appeals. Defense attorneys try to reduce charges, negotiate plea deals, or even get charges dismissed. If the case goes to court, they argue on behalf of their clients and present evidence to defend them. Key Differences Between Criminal Justice Attorneys and Criminal Defense Attorneys There are some important differences between criminal justice attorneys and criminal defense attorneys to take note of: Who They Represent Criminal justice attorneys can represent the government, crime victims, or act as judges. Criminal defense attorneys always represent defendants who are accused of committing crimes. Their Goals in a Case Criminal justice attorneys who are prosecutors want to secure convictions. If representing crime victims, they advocate for justice and fair treatment. Criminal defense attorneys, on the other hand, focus entirely on protecting defendants and achieving the best possible outcome for their clients. Their Roles in Court Criminal justice attorneys might be judges, prosecutors, or victim advocates. Meanwhile, criminal defense attorneys are always in court to defend someone accused of a crime. These differences mean each type of attorney has a unique and specific role within the legal system. Which Attorney Is Right for You? If you’re accused of a crime, you should speak to a criminal defense attorney right away. They specifically handle cases like yours and will ensure your rights are fully protected. If you’re the victim of a crime or want help from someone who represents your interests or the government’s side, a criminal justice attorney who represents victims might be better for you. It’s important to clearly understand your situation and legal rights to pick the right type of attorney. That way, you can get legal help from a qualified professional and set yourself up for a favorable outcome.
